epic_triage_meta.strategy_summary: Execute backend-contracts first to remove deprecated mission wrappers, unify domainSpec/runtime contracts, and tighten game data typing; validate those backend boundary changes before moving on. Then execute gameplay_backend to break down gameActions responsibilities and normalize cache/ping error handling. After those root-cause backend batches, address terminal-side orchestration and docs/dependency/test-harness hygiene, then add targeted validation/tests for the touched seams before the next full rescan.

observe.report: Baseline improved after trusted internal subjective review: strict rose from 23.7 to 60.4. Highest-value themes are missing automated tests across nearly all production modules, oversized orchestration hubs in convex/gameActions.ts and components/GameTerminal.tsx, duplicated command/mission finalization logic, and drift between schema/shared types/domain-spec contracts. Generated PDDL artifacts are not dominating the reviewed queue, so pddl/generated does not currently justify exclusion.
observe.confirmed_text: I have thoroughly reviewed the codebase and the imported findings, including the dominant root-cause dimensions test_strategy, design_coherence, and type_safety, before proceeding to the next planning stage.

reflect.report: The review data points to a few shared root causes rather than isolated defects: gameplay command handling is overly centralized in convex/gameActions.ts, UI command orchestration is concentrated in components/GameTerminal.tsx, and mission/domainSpec/type definitions drift across schema, runtime, and shared types. Because tests are almost absent, the pass should favor structural simplification and contract tightening first, then add just enough validation around the touched seams to keep behavior stable. Low-cost cleanup like deprecated wrappers, noisy comments, and unused dependencies should be folded into those subsystem batches instead of treated as standalone work.
reflect.confirmed_text: I have reflected on the review findings and formed a strategy that prioritizes design_coherence, test_strategy, and type_safety root causes over isolated symptom cleanup.

organize.report: Organized the queue around root-cause batches. Cluster backend-contracts covers missions/domainSpec/gameData/shared-type contract cleanup, and cluster gameplay_backend covers gameActions/cache/ping orchestration cleanup; both are enriched with concrete action steps and should be handled ahead of standalone smell fixes. Terminal UI orchestration remains the next manual batch centered on GameTerminal and supporting components after backend contracts settle, followed by low-cost dependency/comment/deprecation cleanup and then targeted tests for the touched seams.
organize.confirmed_text: I have organized the work into executor-ready batches around design_coherence, type_safety, and test_strategy root causes, with enriched backend-contracts and gameplay_backend clusters sequenced ahead of symptom-level cleanup.

After those root-cause backend batches, address terminal-side orchestration and docs/dependency/test-harness hygiene, then add targeted validation/tests for the touched seams before the next full rescan.
